newsitem.title: GERMANY: BRIGHTER OUTLOOK FOR GERMAN SHARES POST-BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: BRIGHTER OUTLOOK FOR GERMAN SHARES POST-BOURSE.

text.p: German shares were stable in after-bourse electronic dealings on Monday, having put the Wall Street-driven sharp decline of the morning firmly behind them.
Dealers said the broad market outlook seemed lightly positive, with U.S. stocks expected to post minor gains, Bunds firm and with the dollar holding its own against the mark.

The 30-share IBIS DAX was down 6.19 points at 4,336.12 points at 1303 GMT, marking a mild recovery from the mid-afternoon bourse session close at 4,333.13 points and more than 60 points off an intraday low of 4,267.74 points.
September DTB DAX futures were up eight at 4,353.0.
"The market's been holding up remarkably well," said one Frankfurt dealer.
"These rumours in the banking and steel sectors are really helping to keep the momentum going."
Talk of a merger between the allied steelmakers Thyssen AG and Krupp, and persistent speculation that Commerzbank AG is poised to be taken over, were the big stories on the bourse.
Thyssen, commenting on a report in the respected Spiegel magazine which said a fusion may be imminent, said a merger with Krupp was "imaginable".
Thyssen was up 7.20 marks at 422.90 marks in afternoon trade while Krupp was up 6.10 marks at 327 marks.

Meanwhile a mega-merger in the Swiss financial services sector between Credit Suisse and insurer Winterthur fired renewed interest in shares in Commerzbank AG, which repeatedly comes into the spotlight as a takeover target.
Commerzbank co-operates with Winterthur in Germany and the merger revived talk it might be taken over from Switzerland.
The bank's shares were up 5.28 percent at 69.64 marks.
"The rumour mill is grinding again," said one Frankfurt dealer.
Dealers also liked six-month earnings from tyre-maker Continental AG, which reported a 73 percent profit jump.
Continental shares were up four percent at 49.99 marks in IBISD trade.

On the downside, shares in pharmaceuticals group Altana AG remained sharply lower after the company confirmed market speculation that it had ceased developing a successor to its Pantoprazol stomach ulcer drug.
Analysts said this would have minimal impact on earnings in the mid-term but could be negative in the longer term.
Altana shares were down 19.50 marks, or 12 percent, at 143.50 marks in the afternoon, but were well above a low hit of 136 marks.

"It looks as though even Altana isn't getting the major routing it looked like getting earlier today," commented a trader. "But this news has taken a lot of the imaginative attraction from the stock."
Volumes were moderate in other shares, dealers said.
The rest of the week's prime focus was expected to be the start of the chemical sector half-year earnings reporting season with Henkel KGaA data due on Tuesday.
Chemical shares were generally stable to lower on Monday afternoon with Hoechst AG down 10 pfennigs at 83.20 marks and BASF AG down 30 pfennigs at 71.30 marks.
Analysts are expecting that all the large chemicals groups will show they are profiting from the weakness of the mark and strong foreign demand.
BASF is expected to report the best sales and earnings of its history while Bayer is seen with slightly more modest advances.
--Catherine O'Mahony, Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525
